findings.title: `fire_unit_until` cannot stop the firing early — `mt-run` already blocks until the unit exits
findings.description:
The whole point of this change (#22) is stated in the docstring: "a minute firing is unbounded … a cutover that waits for the unit to END waits for days. It waits for the line it needs instead," and the inline comment in `cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:176-179` says "the unit is stopped once that line lands and the timers own the backfill."

That cannot happen. `deploy/mt-run`'s `start_and_stream` runs `systemctl start --no-block` and then blocks in `while is_running "${unit}"; do sleep 2; done` until the unit exits, exiting with its code. `run(...)` here is a synchronous `subprocess.run`, so line 356 (`run(["mt-run", *mt_run_args], sudo=True, check=False, stream=True)`) returns only *after* the pass has ended. By the time control reaches `wait_for_unit_or_line` (line 357), `unit_active(unit)` is False, the loop body never executes, and `stop_unit` (line 360) is unreachable in production. `mt-minute-pass.service` carries `TimeoutStartSec=infinity`, so the blocking wait is exactly the days-long wait the change exists to avoid.

The test cannot catch this: `test_the_minute_firing_stops_once_the_trailing_phase_completes` (`test/unit/test_cutover_921.py:482`) patches `cutover_common.run` to a `MagicMock` and drives `unit_active` from a hand-written list, so the real blocking contract of `mt-run` is never exercised. Either `mt-run` needs a non-blocking start verb, or the stop must be driven from a separate process/watchdog rather than after the blocking call.

findings.title: A `[WAIT]` verdict in the firing loop spends another ~65k credits instead of waiting
findings.description: `verify_text = _verify_when_fresh()`; `[WAIT]` means the cagg has not materialized the bars yet, not that trailing work remains. But the loop only breaks on `"FAIL" not in verify_text and "[WAIT]" not in verify_text`, so a WAIT falls through to the next iteration and fires another minute pass. `_verify_when_fresh` already polls for up to `VERIFY_WAIT_SECONDS * VERIFY_WAIT_POLLS` = 75 minutes before returning WAIT, and each additional firing costs on the order of 13k symbols × 5 credits (the script's own `MIN_CREDITS_TO_START` docstring quotes ~65,000 for one trailing phase). The script's stated design is that it "refuses rather than letting the passes produce acceptance numbers that measure a starved account"; a WAIT should end the loop (or pause without firing), not trigger a re-fire.

findings.title: The sudoers alias grants root systemctl on *any* `mt-*` unit, contradicting its own stated scope
findings.description:
The header says "Exactly the commands those scripts issue, nothing wider; every one is a named unit …". `MT_UNITS` is not a set of named units — it is the shell-glob wildcard `mt-*`, so the operator account gets passwordless `stop`/`start`/`restart`/`is-active` over every unit matching that prefix, including `mt-serve.service`, `mt-health.service`, `mt-kalshi-pass.service`, `mt-daily-pass.service` and `manta-acquisition.slice`. The scripts actually need `stop`/`start` on `mt-minute-pass.timer` / `mt-daily-pass.timer` and `stop` on `mt-minute-pass.service` (`cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:160,170` and `cutover_common.stop_unit`). Per the project's "GRANT minimum required privileges" rule, enumerate those units rather than the glob, or correct the comment so the file does not claim a narrower grant than it makes.

Two related notes on the same file: `MT_INSTALL` pins `/home/manta/source/repos/manta/trading-data/deploy/install-production.sh` while `cutover_common.install` derives the path at runtime from `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` — the two must agree exactly and nothing checks that they do; and `MT_READ` grants passwordless root read of `/etc/manta-trading.env`, which is needed by the documented workflow but is a standing credential-exposure grant worth naming explicitly in the file's rationale.

findings.title: `cagg_freshness_for_session` does not normalize `'-infinity'` in `last_successful_finish`
findings.description:
The query selects `stats.last_successful_finish` raw. The repository documents twice, with measurements, that a policy which has been created but never run stores `'-infinity'` there and that psycopg refuses to load it with a `DataError` ("timestamp too small (before year 1)") — see `src/manta_trading/market/maintenance/cagg_freshness.py:68-79`, which wraps it in `nullif(..., '-infinity'::timestamptz)` precisely for this reason, and `test/integration/test_policy_advances_head.py:86-91`, which repeats the normalization with a comment describing the same exception.

This probe is called from `run_verify` (`scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py:276`) with no exception handling around it, so on a database whose `minute_4hour_ohlcv` refresh policy has not yet completed a run, `--verify` dies with a psycopg traceback instead of reporting anything. The same `nullif` normalization used by the existing guard is the fix.

findings.title: The minute-pass timer's description no longer matches the schedule it describes
findings.description: Moving the first firing from 01:05 to 04:05 broke the standing invariant that the file itself asserts: `Description=Fire the minute acquisition pass (staggered 30 min behind the daily pass)`. `mt-daily-pass.timer` fires at 00:35/12:35; 13:05 is still 30 minutes behind 12:35, but 04:05 is 3 h 30 min behind 00:35. The diff corrected the sibling comment in `deploy/systemd/mt-kalshi-pass.timer` to `(00:35/12:35, 04:05/13:05)` but left this file's Description stating a relationship that is now only half true. The two passes still do not collide, so this is a correctness-of-documentation issue rather than a scheduling one — but the sentence is what an operator reads to decide whether the stagger holds.

findings.title: New imports in `minute.py` violate the configured isort ordering
findings.description: `pyproject.toml` selects `I` in `[tool.ruff.lint]`, and the import block added here is not sorted: `manta_trading.data.acquisition.daemon.minute_sessions` is placed *after* `manta_trading.data.gaps`, and `manta_trading.data.gaps.repair_921` is placed *before* `manta_trading.data.gaps.minute_coverage`. The same drift appears in `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:45-59`, where `NOTES_DIR`, `fire_unit_until` and `start_log` were prepended ahead of `CutoverError` in an otherwise sorted list. Both would be rewritten by `ruff check --fix`.

findings.title: The added per-chunk `fetch_session_bounds` round trip is not exercised by a load test
findings.description: Every chunk in the minute loop now opens a pool connection and issues an additional `trading_sessions` lookup before accounting. This is on the acquisition path, where the project's rules call for a load test asserting a resource bound. The slice does have one load test (`test/load/test_921_minute_session_mass_nfr.py`), but it covers the health check's mass read, not the daemon chunk loop; `test/load/test_146_part1_nfrs.py` and `test/load/test_146_part2_nfrs.py` substitute a stub `minute_fn` rather than the real loop. At one extra round trip per chunk across ~13k symbols this is unlikely to matter, but nothing bounds it either way.

findings.title: Per-session chunk judgement and truncated-day seeding are correct and well covered
findings.description: `judge_chunk_by_sessions` / `sessions_without_bars` implement exactly the predicate the docstring claims — a bar strictly after the open and at or before the close — and it matches the repair's truncation signature (`max(time) <= session_open_utc`). The bisect over sorted stamps is right, sessions the chunk cuts through are correctly excluded, and `test/unit/data/acquisition/daemon/test_minute_sessions.py` pins the boundary cases (bar at the open fails, bar at the close passes, spillover-only fails, weekend tail promotes to SUCCESS) including the D-1-bars case that produced the 2026-09-10 truncation. The matching daemon-side tests for `uncovered_days` threading and the `RepairScanTimeout` fail-safe are equally direct, and `_build_truncated_index` logs at ERROR and degrades to "seed without it" rather than reporting an unmeasured universe as clean.

findings.title: The UTC label fix in `check_minute_session_mass` is right
findings.description: Formatting `session_open_utc` / `session_close_utc` through `.astimezone(UTC)` before `%H:%M` is the same pattern `health.py`'s `check_raw_freshness` already uses and for the same reason (a timestamptz arrives in the connection's zone, so the old code would have printed local hours under a "UTC" suffix). The comment names the concrete symptom this prevents.

The minute-pass timer's description no longer matches the schedule it describes
New imports in `minute.py` violate the configured isort ordering
The added per-chunk `fetch_session_bounds` round trip is not exercised by a load test
Per-session chunk judgement and truncated-day seeding are correct and well covered
